name: dots.ocr
purpose: One VLM for layout detection and content recognition of document pages, switched by prompt; multilingual.

license.name: MIT (card tag) plus dots.ocr LICENSE AGREEMENT (custom, MIT prevails on conflict)
license.notes: Agreement text read (repo file "dots.ocr LICENSE AGREEMENT"): grants commercial use and redistribution, but section 3.3 prohibits extracting sensitive personal data (ID numbers, medical records) without legal basis, "unauthorized digitization of publications/document scanning or bulk scraping", and 5.2 prohibits processing GDPR/HIPAA-protected personal data without consent and safeguards; terminates automatically on breach. Card says plain MIT; the agreement adds use limits that matter for invoices and scans of personal documents.

architecture.why_this_design: A single model replaces separate layout and recognition stages (card).

benchmarks.name: MORE German overall (per-language, 149 languages)
benchmarks.harness: read through a summarizer; MORE overall 84.31, table 39.81

weaknesses: complex tables and formulas not yet handled well
can loop on long runs of dots or underscores
not tuned for high-throughput bulk PDFs
MORE (independent): table score only 39.81 over 149 languages
soft.maturity: from July 2025, overtaken on OmniDocBench by newer models; no newer version found on the card

tona_fit.reason: solid German evidence (MDPBench DE 79.7, MORE de 94.2) but superseded by dots.mocr (same license, higher scores) and its license agreement restricts personal-data and scanned-publication use, which collides with typical document-analysis jobs

open_questions: a legal reading of the agreement clauses 3.3(b)/(c) and 5.2 for local, private use by an individual

sources.note: MDPBench README table read directly; an earlier summarizer pass mislabeled the Latin-average column as DE, the DE values here come from the dataset README

pc-16gb.notes: BF16 about 2 GB; Tona runs one model at a time, so it replaces the resident model while it works
